evidence.reason: Ready() returns Ready whose Messages field carries outbound pb.Message instances; acceptReady sets raft.msgs = nil, transferring exclusive ownership to the caller and making the caller's slice the only retention point.
rd.Messages = r.msgs moves the outbound message slice out of the raft state machine before delivery; nothing delivers automatically, so delivery resumes only on a later test action.
InteractionEnv owns the in-flight message cache as the exported field Messages []pb.Message and Nodes []Node, i.e. an env-owned capture cache around public RawNode objects.
ProcessReady drains a node's Ready, appends non-local Messages to env.Messages (and local MsgStorageAppend/Apply to AppendWork/ApplyWork), and calls Advance, i.e. the harness-side capture step.
DeliverMsgs removes from env.Messages all messages matching recipient+type and delivers or drops them; it is a bulk filter over matching values, not an exact-instance Take/Drop API.

message_capture.gap: No path provides a complete capture cache. Direct paths: Ready.Messages/Ready-channel hand the message instances to the test, but the retaining collection is caller-created and all Take/Drop/Clear logic must be hand-written. rafttest path: env.Messages is an env-owned cache with enumeration and bulk DeliverMsgs/Drop by recipient+type, but exact-instance Take, exact-instance Drop, and Clear are missing.
message_capture.reason: All three discovered paths retain controlled protocol output before delivery (Ready.Messages is moved out of the raft state machine; rafttest moves it into env.Messages), but none exposes a complete capture cache: the direct RawNode/Node paths hand messages to a caller-created slice (an explicit primitive), and rafttest's env.Messages is only manipulated through bulk recipient/type DeliverMsgs without exact-instance Take/Drop/Clear operations. The missing cache operations are low-intrusion additions that do not change protocol semantics.
limitations: Ready.Entries and Ready.CommittedEntries alias the unstable log's backing array until stableTo/applyCommittedEntries; the documented read-only rule on Ready fields is not a safe snapshot for mutation, so capture claims cover Ready.Messages only.

pb.Message values contain slice fields (Entries, Context, Responses); when a cached message is later stepped into another node, raft log entries alias the message's entry data (append copies struct values but not Data payloads).

In AsyncStorageWrites mode the local-thread messages (MsgStorageAppend/MsgStorageApply) are captured separately in AppendWork/ApplyWork and their Responses re-enter env.Messages; this remains part of the same rafttest route.
message_capture.suggested_direction: Extend rafttest with a small cache facade (Take/Drop/Clear over env.Messages) and add an equivalent thin wrapper for direct RawNode/Node driving; both are additive and do not alter protocol behavior.
message_capture.test_support_reason: The capture mechanics (output retained before delivery, single consumer, no racing) are already correct on all paths, but the cache operations are not: the direct paths expose a raw output collection (caller-created slice, explicitly a primitive per the contract), and rafttest exposes only bulk recipient/type selection plus an exported slice that the consumer would have to hand-edit for exact-instance Take/Drop/Clear.
suggested_changes: Add exported exact-instance cache operations to rafttest over env.Messages, e.g. TakeMsg(pred func(raftpb.Message) bool) (raftpb.Message, bool) removing and returning one selected message with its routing fields, DropMsgs(pred), and ClearMessages(), keeping DeliverMsgs as the combined delivery call.

Add a thin exported capture wrapper for the direct paths (e.g. in rafttest: a Driver type wrapping *raft.RawNode that owns a message cache populated from Ready().Messages with Take/Drop/Clear and Advance), so the RawNode and Node direct routes gain a complete capture interface without changing protocol semantics.
Optionally export an exact-instance helper that preserves message order and reports the target node index/id for each taken message so the test can map to its own runtime objects.
execution_paths: RawNode direct drive: output = rn.Ready().Messages (ownership transferred, r.msgs cleared); no automatic delivery; continuation via rn.Advance(rd). Cache = caller-held slice (primitive; enumerate by index, Take/Drop/Clear hand-written). Input boundary = rn.Step; target = test-owned RawNode instances; routing via m.To/m.From.

evidence.reason: Draws randomizedElectionTimeout = electionTimeout + globalRand.Intn(electionTimeout); the value gates election start (pastElectionTimeout) and is reset on follower/candidate transitions.
globalRand is a shared crypto/rand source (rand.Reader) with no seeding or injection point from Config.
The only setter is exported but defined in a _test.go file (package raft); it is compiled only for the module's own tests and is not callable by external consumers of the module.

rafttest exposes a hook for setting the timeout, but an external consumer cannot implement it because it requires access to unexported raft state; the module's own test plumbs it with the test-file-only function (interaction_test.go:32).

randomness_control.gap: Election-timeout draws come from globalRand (crypto/rand, raft.go:2050) with no exported setter or seed for consumers; the drawn value is not exposed by Status or Ready; rafttest's InteractionOpts.SetRandomizedElectionTimeout hook has no externally implementable implementation (raft.SetRandomizedElectionTimeout is test-file-only).
randomness_control.reason: The only protocol-relevant randomness is the randomized election timeout drawn from a shared crypto/rand-backed global source (resetRandomizedElectionTimeout), which cannot be seeded, set, or observed by an external consumer: the only setter (raft.SetRandomizedElectionTimeout) lives in raft_test.go and is unavailable to module consumers, and the rafttest InteractionOpts hook cannot be implemented from outside the package. Exposing the draw as a public setter/hook is a low-intrusion change that preserves the production default.
limitations: Non-protocol randomness (network drop/delay in the unexported rafttest/network.go harness, send-delay sleeps in rafttest/node.go) is out of the protocol boundary or setup-only and is not counted.
The draw value is not exposed by Status/BasicStatus/Ready, so without a setter the test cannot learn the selected value before scheduling dependent work.
Randomization is reset on every follower/candidate transition; reproducible control must cover each reset.
randomness_control.suggested_direction: Expose the existing test-only setter as a production RawNode method (or a Config hook) so external consumers can supply deterministic election-timeout draws; keep globalRand as the default source.
randomness_control.test_support_reason: The election-timeout draw is protocol-relevant (gates elections), but no externally callable interface exists: the rafttest hook cannot be implemented without internal access, the production source is shared crypto/rand, and the drawn value is not observable, so the test can neither supply nor learn each draw.
suggested_changes: Move SetRandomizedElectionTimeout from raft_test.go into production as an exported method on RawNode (rawnode.go), preserving the exact semantics; this makes the rafttest InteractionOpts hook implementable by external consumers and lets the test supply (and therefore know) each draw.

Alternatively, add a Config-level injection point for the election-timeout draw (e.g. a func(electionTick int) int field or a seedable source) that defaults to the current globalRand behavior, keeping the production default unchanged.
Document the per-node scope and legal domain: values should remain within [ElectionTick, 2*ElectionTick-1] or be validated as the target validates them.
execution_paths: Election timeout randomization (all drive paths): the raft runtime draws randomizedElectionTimeout from globalRand on becoming follower/candidate; the draw determines when tickElection fires MsgHup, so it controls which node becomes candidate and when. Same behavior under RawNode direct drive, Node channel drive, and rafttest env drive.

evidence.reason: Advances the internal logical clock by exactly one tick synchronously (rn.raft.tick()), the directly testable Tick on the RawNode path.
Nonblocking send into tickc (cap 128) with a default branch that drops the tick when the run loop is blocked, logging 'A tick missed to fire'; requested advances can be lost.
env.Tick(idx,num) calls the embedded RawNode.Tick num times; exact and synchronous on the harness path.
tickElection increments electionElapsed and fires MsgHup once past the randomized election timeout; tickHeartbeat drives heartbeats and check-quorum — the protocol transitions driven by Tick.

time_control.gap: Node.Tick (node.go:463-470) sends into tickc with a default branch that drops the tick and logs 'A tick missed to fire' when the buffer is full; the Node-driven path therefore does not guarantee that a requested advance is accepted and applied. RawNode.Tick and rafttest Tick(idx,num) are exact.
time_control.reason: RawNode.Tick and the rafttest Tick handler are exact, synchronous, deterministic logical-clock advances that drive electionElapsed/heartbeatElapsed and produce protocol transitions (tickElection/tickHeartbeat); there is no wall clock in the protocol itself. However, Node.Tick on the channel-driven path is a nonblocking send into a 128-slot buffer that drops ticks with only a warning when the run loop is busy, so a requested advance is not guaranteed to be applied on that path. Making that path lossless is a low-intrusion change that preserves timer ordering and transition conditions.
limitations: Node.Tick drops ticks (with a warning) when 128 ticks are buffered; tests must keep the run loop drained or use RawNode.Tick for guaranteed advances.

The unexported internal network harness (rafttest/node.go) drives nodes from a real time.Ticker (5ms) and randomized send sleeps; it is same-package-only and its wall-clock behavior is outside the protocol time path.
Randomized election timeout still determines when a ticked election actually starts (see randomness_control), so exact tick counts do not by themselves manufacture an election outcome.
time_control.suggested_direction: Remove or acknowledge the drop in Node.Tick so every claimed path applies each requested advance deterministically; RawNode and rafttest Tick already satisfy this.
time_control.test_support_reason: The protocol time model is a purely logical clock with no wall-clock dependency, and RawNode.Tick plus rafttest Tick provide exact deterministic advances; only the Node-interface Tick is a nonblocking surface that can drop a requested advance, so the Node-driven path is not complete.
suggested_changes: Make Node.Tick lossless: remove the default drop branch (block until the run loop consumes or the node is stopped), preserving the buffered channel for normal operation and keeping production tick ordering and transition conditions.

Alternatively add a synchronous tick confirmation (e.g. an optional interface with TickAndWait or draining tickc before returning) so the Node path guarantees each requested advance is applied deterministically.
Keep RawNode.Tick as the documented exact surface and have rafttest Tick continue delegating to it.
execution_paths: RawNode direct drive: rn.Tick() is a synchronous, deterministic advance; election and heartbeat transitions fire deterministically on the next Ready.

Node channel drive: n.Tick() posts to a buffered channel consumed by the run loop; exact when the loop keeps up, but drops ticks (with a warning) when the buffer is full, so advances are not guaranteed.
rafttest InteractionEnv: env.Tick(idx,num) calls RawNode.Tick exactly num times; deterministic advance used by tick-election/tick-heartbeat commands.
